parakeet: Why don't you attack Islam or other religions? Why don't you rate the story you've never shopped at? This is a two quo qui fallacy, or whataboutism as well. Deflects criticism by pointing to others. Why don't you go after them rather than addressing the issue at hand? Now, what it reveals is that this isn't about concern for fairness, it's about deflection. It tries to flip the focus from the critique at hand and turn the critic into the problem. It reveals a subtle demand for religious exceptionalism, a belief that Christianity deserves special immunity from scrutiny. And when it's challenged, that feels like persecution, not conversation. Now the harm, which I shouldn't even have to speak to, but this mindset shuts down meaningful dialogue and stokes a victim complex. It trains people to see critical thinking as an attack and self-reflection as betrayal. It also weaponizes comparative suffering, as if Christianity can only be held accountable after every other religion is critiqued first. That fuels tribalism, not truth. Deep down, you still believe. Deep down you don't believe? See, this fallacy is begging the question and it's also appealed to ignorance. It assumes belief is innate and inescapable, begs the question, and argues from the lack of disproof. You can't prove you don't still believe in the same way that you can't really prove that you believe by that argument. What it reveals is that this statement isn't about you, it's about their unresolved fear. If you can truly stop believing and live a full meaningful life, then their entire system starts to look optional. It reveals a need to externalize doubt to place it on you instead of confronting it within. Because if belief isn't inescapable, then neither is their identity, and that's terrifying.
